lisbonPilot.title: Free tango movement workshops for people with Parkinson's
lisbonPilot.lead: A free pilot for Lisbon care institutions, now through 30 November 2026. Gentle, staff-supervised and adapted to every ability.
lisbonPilot.whyBody: I'm Jean, founder of FreeBrain. I live with dystonia and have managed it with Argentine tango for years, after training in Buenos Aires. I volunteer weekly at Centro de Dia Nossa Senhora (Santa Casa). Most of our Instagram community lives with Parkinson's, and they tell us the hardest part is keeping moving. That is the problem we are working on.
lisbonPilot.offer1: A weekly 45-minute tango movement workshop for motor and cognitive stimulation, led by me and supervised by your staff
lisbonPilot.offer2: Gentle exercises adapted to reduced mobility, with a seated option for everyone
lisbonPilot.offer3: Simple techniques your team can use to activate residents and patients between sessions
lisbonPilot.offer4: An anonymized summary of results at the end of the pilot
lisbonPilot.ask1: A suitable room and at least one qualified staff member present at every session
lisbonPilot.ask2: A 15-minute check-in after each workshop and a short anonymous survey (about 5 minutes)
lisbonPilot.ask3: Consent forms from each participant, and from anyone who is filmed
lisbonPilot.ask4: Confirmation that your institution's liability insurance covers activities on your premises
lisbonPilot.ask5: Optional: permission to share photos and video (with consent) and a short recommendation if you're happy
lisbonPilot.step1: Meet and agree. We review a short agreement together and confirm your insurance details.
lisbonPilot.step2: Weekly sessions. 45 minutes at a day and time that suits your routine, then a quick check-in.
lisbonPilot.step3: Review and leave-behind. We share what we observed and leave you with techniques and early access to the FreeBrain app concept.
lisbonPilot.safetyBody: Movement always carries some risk, so we plan for it. Your staff stay responsible for safety and medical decisions, and I will adapt or stop any activity at any time. Anyone with high fall risk can sit, watch only or sit out. Taking part is voluntary, and filming only happens with written consent. These workshops are a movement activity, not medical treatment, and they don't replace anyone's care.
lisbonPilot.safetyNote: Either side can stop with 7 days' notice. There are no fees of any kind.
lisbonPilot.appBody: FreeBrain is a mobile app concept designed to help caregivers and staff fit short, fun movement breaks into daily routines, with no complex training. It is still early, and your team's feedback will shape it. We intend to offer it to you as a leave-behind after the pilot, with no obligation.
lisbonPilot.summitBody: FreeBrain is exhibiting as an Alpha Startup. We're inviting a small group of Lisbon institutions to send one representative to our booth for a day to join the movement demonstrations and show the world what Lisbon is doing for movement therapy.
lisbonPilot.nextBody: Tell me a day that works and I'll bring the one-page agreement.

evidence.title: Supporting Evidence
evidence.subtitle: Explore the research and clinical studies that form the foundation of our movement therapy approach.

items.1: High-intensity exercise induces brain-protective effects that have the potential to not just slow down, but possibly reverse, the neurodegeneration associated with Parkinson's disease, a new pilot study suggests.
items.2: Dance, in fact, has such beneficial effects on the brain that it is now being used to treat people with Parkinson's disease
items.3: The right kind of treatment and rehabilitation programs can help promote neuroplasticity
items.4: therapeutic dancing can be beneficial for improving motor performance and balance in people with PD
items.5: Exercise can help preserve and improve cognitive function and fend off dementia, stroke, depression and anxiety. Aim for 150 minutes per week.
